_comment: Events happening in or near the forest. Manually researched and verified on lastVerified; not yet fed by an automated script (see spec/spec-weekly-report.md).

entries.title: Epping Forest Wildwood Trail Series: Half Marathon & 10K
entries.body: A trail half marathon (9:00 start) and 10K (9:30 start) through Epping Forest, chip-timed, with aid stations and limited parking. Entry around £37, ages 17+.

entries.title: Top Picks: litter pick at Hollow Ponds
entries.body: Free, volunteer-run litter pick at Hollow Ponds, part of the Epping Forest charity's recurring 'Top Picks' series.

entries.title: Apple Day at Copped Hall
entries.body: Family event in the Mansion and gardens at Copped Hall: apple identification by an orchard expert, produce and plant stalls, live music (Chingford Morris Men, Harlow Brass Band) and children's entertainment. Gates open 11am, last entry 4pm. Tickets £12 in advance or £15 on the day; free for Friends of Copped Hall, under-18s and carers.

entries.title: Archives on Show: Epping Forest
entries.place: The London Archives, 40 Northampton Road, EC1R 0HB
entries.body: Free, one-hour drop-in sessions (1pm or 2pm) on Epping Forest's archives, run on multiple dates. Check the listing for the next date -- none is reliably current as of this verification.
entries.reverificationNote: No specific upcoming date confirmed -- re-check the listing for the next session before using in a report.

sourceNotes.source: City of London: Epping Forest & Commons Committee (EFCC) 'Committee Events Diary'
sourceNotes.note: The single best structured events source found: a detailed month-by-month diary (exhibitions, guided tours, litter picks, youth conservation sessions, volunteering) published as a PDF alongside each committee meeting's agenda pack on democracy.cityoflondon.gov.uk. No stable URL -- a new PDF is published at each meeting (next: 2026-11-02), so a script would need to find the committee's current agenda page (search 'Epping Forest Commons Committee' on democracy.cityoflondon.gov.uk) and pull the latest 'Diary' attachment. Worth building a scraper for.

sourceNotes.source: Eventbrite organiser 'Epping Forest' (collections: Festive Forest, Top Picks, Leaky Dam Building)
sourceNotes.note: Real and current, but an API key would not improve on scraping the public pages: Eventbrite retired public cross-organiser event search from its v3 API in February 2020. The remaining API only lists events for an organisation/account you yourself control (GET /v3/organizations/{id}/events/) -- there's no approval tier that reopens access to another organiser's calendar, and 'Epping Forest' is not our account. An OAuth app (the application URL + redirect URI Eventbrite's developer portal asks for) buys nothing here. Scraping the public collection pages, as done for this file, remains the only option.

Good general-interest page (reminders, long-running works, car park/riding/fishing notices -- see data/forest-notices.json) but it's a single long page with no dates on most items and no RSS feed, so it suits a human skim better than automated diffing.

District council activities (not City of London / forest-specific) with no dates or locations on the page itself -- detail is locked in a brochure PDF. Lower value for forest-specific events than the EFCC diary.

sourceNotes.source: coppedhalltrust.org.uk (own site, e.g. the Apple Day article)
sourceNotes.note: Copped Hall is independently run by its own trust, not City of London, so it never appears in the EFCC diary above -- this is the first entry sourced from a venue-specific site rather than a forest-wide aggregator. It's a plain CMS article per event, no calendar index or RSS found, so a script would have no list of 'current article ids' to crawl; finding new events still means someone (or the weekly research step) visiting the site. Worth re-checking each run rather than building a scraper for yet. The same is likely true of other independently-run sites inside or near the boundary (visitor centres, heritage trusts) that this run hasn't individually surveyed.

sourceNotes.source: Facebook pages of forest-adjacent organisations (e.g. Epping Forest Heritage Trust)
sourceNotes.note: Not usable, by API or by scraping. Meta has gated the Graph API's 'Page Public Content Access' behind App Review and Business Verification since 2018 (post-Cambridge Analytica), so there is no keyless or simple-OAuth way to read an arbitrary public Page's posts. Fetching a post's own URL without being logged in confirms this in practice: the page returns only its title, no post body, date or details. A human can still open the page and read it; nothing here is automatable.

Not usable for free. X removed free read access in 2023; reading another account's posts (search or timeline) now needs at minimum the paid Basic tier, priced per month rather than per use, which is a standing cost for monitoring accounts that mostly repeat what their own websites or Facebook pages already say. Not worth it unless a specific account turns out to be the only place an event is announced.

sourceNotes.source: Wanstead Village Directory events calendar (wansteadvillagedirectory.com/events/ -- covers Wanstead and Wanstead Park, the forest's southern tip)
sourceNotes.note: A real, directly-fetchable, VERIFIED source: its WordPress 'The Events Calendar' plugin exposes a plain iCal feed at https://wansteadvillagedirectory.com/events/list/?ical=1 -- fetched and parsed on 2026-10-10 and confirmed to contain an actual VEVENT for 'Wanstead Beer Festival 2026' (DTSTART 2026-10-10T13:00 Europe/London, at Christ Church Hall, Wanstead), the event that went unnoticed and prompted this evaluation (github.com/simonmcmanus/epping-forest-finds/issues/192). This supersedes an earlier, unverified note in this file pointing at a different Wanstead calendar (Wansteadium's, run through a public Google Calendar) which was never actually confirmed to carry the festival -- don't resurrect that one without verifying its content first.

The official Epping Forest District tourism site. A plain page with no feed, but its event list (dates, venue, description) is present in the raw HTML rather than requiring JavaScript, so it scrapes the same way Copped Hall's site does. Broader than any single town's listing: covers venues across the whole district, including Copped Hall and Epping Ongar Railway.
A plain page (Town Show, Christmas Market, Remembrance services, Monday Market) with no feed, same treatment as Copped Hall's site: worth checking by hand each run, not yet worth a scraper.

sourceNotes.source: Epping Ongar Railway (eorailway.co.uk) -- heritage railway in the district running galas and a Real Ale and Cider Weekend
sourceNotes.note: A real, forest-district-relevant venue, but eorailway.co.uk returned HTTP 503 to a direct automated fetch (both the events page and the site root) -- likely bot-blocking rather than the site being down, since the same content is reachable via search-engine caches and third-party listings (raildays.org). Covered indirectly via the Visit Epping Forest calendar above for now; worth re-testing eorailway.co.uk directly on a future run in case the block lifts.

sourceNotes.source: Loughton Town Council, Waltham Abbey Town Council 'What's On', Waltham Forest borough-wide listings (which would cover Chingford), and Theydon Bois Parish Council's events category page
sourceNotes.note: No usable feed found for any of the four, and no current, dated events listing confirmed as of this evaluation -- Loughton's site surfaces only its news section (most recent dated item from 2025), Waltham Abbey's calendar is advertised as email-submission-only with no feed, Waltham Forest's borough events listing is paginated HTML with no RSS/Atom link found and nothing specific to Chingford, and Theydon Bois PC's 'Events' category is actually news-style posts by publish date, not event date, with the newest confirmed-dated item (an exhibition) from January 2023. Re-check each run rather than building automation against any of them yet; a council could add a feed at any time.
